title: A zoomed recording's motion path shows where the camera points, or nothing
goal: When a recording is zoomed in and its framing is keyed, the canvas draws a dashed path for the move that follows the corner of the clip, a line across empty canvas that has nothing to do with where the camera is pointing. It should show the route of the centre, or not be drawn on a recording at all.
notes: Seen 2026-10-09 by a-recording-s-framing-reads-as-scale-then-centre. Repro: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/framing-a-zoom-keys-its-centre-walk.json, pictures 3-framed-at-5-sc.png and 3b-centre-typed-sc.png show a dashed route from about (846,400) to (1465,633) screen points over the dark canvas, which is the posed origin path of the Position motion (copies under queue/audits/2026-10-09-zoom-centre-3-framed-at-5-sc.png). The video-zoom-wt mock draws no path in steps 6-8, only the frame ring. Which of the two (centre route or none) is a UX call; a decision card if unsure. Path drawing: grep motion path / route in Sources/Photonz canvas overlays; position on a takesAReframe layer is Layer.positionReadsAsCentre.
acceptance: With Scale and Centre keyed on a recording, the dashed path on the canvas either follows the point in the middle of the frame or is not drawn
A title or shape keyed on Position still draws its path exactly as today
A walk at Next defaults photographs the canvas with the zoom framed

log.note: Full Scripts/test.sh hung at 0% CPU after 10 min, swiftpm-testing-helper parked in VNRecognizeTextRequest and CGImageDestinationFinalize: the signature already on find-out-why-the-whole-test-run-hangs-in-the-mac. Killed it, ran the split that task records instead.

Adversarial pass: the centre route has no honest home on the canvas. The camera always points at the middle of the frame, so a centre route drawn in the recording's own points would land on features that are not where the magnified picture shows them. The zoom mock draws no path in steps 6-8 and no Path row, so the mock settles it: no path, no card needed. A Premiere user sees the same: the Program monitor shows no Position path for Scale-to-crop zooms in Screen Studio-style tools.

Built: PhotonzDocument.motionPath(layerID:) returns nil when layer.positionReadsAsCentre (MotionPath.swift); EditorState.motionPathShape nil for the same, so the Path row and the Video menu's Curve the Path (disabled) follow. Tests: RecordingFramingReadsAsCentreTests +2 (recording draws none, title still draws). Walk framing-a-zoom-keys-its-centre-walk now expects no Path row after the framed shot; it passes with 6 real captures. motion-path-walk, between-the-keys-walk, every-title-dropdown-opens-on-a-click-walk pass unchanged (they key a title over the recording).

Rough edge filed: the picked zoomed recording is outlined as the whole magnified box, so a dashed edge and handle hang off the frame, where the mock rings the frame: a-zoomed-recording-shows-its-ring-on-the-frame-n. Left rough, no task: a recording that already carries a bend from before keeps it, invisibly, with no Path row to straighten it; nobody could easily bend one before and no mock asks for it.

Correction to the adversarial note above: Premiere does draw a Position path in the Program monitor for a clip's Motion; the case for none here is the mock and that a reframe's Position is the camera, not the clip moving.

A framed recording draws no motion path and no Path row (matches video-zoom-wt steps 6-8); titles and shapes keep their path. MotionPath.swift + EditorState+MotionPath.swift, 2 new core tests, framing-a-zoom-keys-its-centre-walk expects no Path row and passes at Next defaults with 6 real captures; motion-path, between-the-keys and title-dropdown walks pass. Audit 2026-10-11-zoomed-recording-draws-no-motion-path.json. Commit 849bce62.
